To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we determined a 2D‐structure model of the Yjb adaptor protein by crosslinking MS, which was validated by a combination of experimental and computational approaches.
(i) YjbH is a DsbA‐family protein; (ii) the N‐terminal arm is flexible and can interact with Spx; and (iii) the core structure of YbjH interacts with Spx.
the bacterial adaptor protein, YjbH, has a thioredoxin‐like fold and interacts with Spx at two distinct sites.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure and interactions of a protein that is involved in a complex network of interactions.
the structure and function of bacterial proteins that are involved in stress responses and the regulation of gene expression.
understanding the molecular basis of how YjbH interacts with its substrate Spx.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the structure and interactions of YjbH were investigated by chemical crosslinking and mass spectrometry, which provided valuable information about the structure of the protein and its interactions with other molecules, and which was used to validate a structure model and to propose a model for the interactions of Yjb H with the transcription factor Spx.
crosslinking mass-spectrometry has been used to gain insight into the structure of the adaptor protein Yjb H and its interactions with the protease and substrate.
crosslinking mass spectroscopy is a powerful technique to investigate the structure of a protein in the absence of its crystalline structure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the structure of Yjb H is very similar to that of a thioredoxin‐like protein and that the N‐terminal part of Yjb H can interact with Spx and that this interaction can stabilize the Spx protein for protease degradation.
we were able to identify a number of residues in the YjbH protein that are important for interaction with the Spx protein.
the crosslinking mass spectroscopy (XL‐MS) approach can be used to gain insight into protein structure and interactions, in the absence of high‐resolution structures of the proteins of interest.
The main takeaway from our work is that
chemical crosslinking can be used to gain insight into the structure and interactions of proteins.
chemical crosslinking can provide useful information about the structure and interactions of proteins.
crosslinking mass spectroscopy can be used to obtain information on the structure of proteins that are difficult to crystallize or to study by other methods.
